task.description:
Hard gate on CODE-DESIGNER's design at lib/letflow/design/iss0451-poller-crash-budget-isolation.md. Independently re-derive your verdict from the artefact itself, not from CODE-DESIGNER's own result.summary (which you should treat as a claim to verify, not a fact to copy) -- see core-directives.md's 'Every producing step has a validating step'. Check specifically:
1. Does the design cover every one of ISS-0451's three acceptance criteria (docs/issues/ISS-0451.yaml): AC1 (a persistent-fault test scenario proving Letflow.Supervisor/Repo/Bandit survive), AC2 (documented restart-intensity arithmetic showing the fix tolerates at least one full Pollers-budget-exhaustion cycle), AC3 (no regression to REQ-219's own AC2 boot-order or AC4 single-crash-isolation tests)?
2. Is the arithmetic in the design actually correct? Work it through yourself rather than trusting the doc's own numbers -- re-derive independently whether the chosen top-level restart-intensity value plus the circuit-breaker's trip threshold genuinely prevents an indefinite persistent fault from ever exhausting the top-level supervisor's budget (not merely delaying it by a bounded, finite number of extra cycles).
3. Does the design contain any implementation code (.ex function bodies)? If it names a new module (e.g. a PollersBreaker GenServer), it should specify signatures/@specs/state-shape/callback contracts only -- fail this check if you find an actual function body implementing logic, not just a signature.
4. Is the design unambiguous enough for ELIXIR-DEV to implement without having to invent any missing decision (exact config keys, exact state machine transitions, exact backoff schedule values, exact module/file placement)?
5. Does the design explicitly state how REQ-219's own AC2 (boot order: Infrastructure before Pollers) and AC4 (single Pollers-budget-exhaustion event still leaves Infrastructure/Http alone) are preserved, with reasoning you can independently verify against the current code (lib/letflow/application.ex, lib/letflow/supervisor/pollers.ex)?
6. Is the specified regression-test mechanism (how the test keeps the fault persistent, unlike REQ-219's own AC4 test which clears it) concrete enough for TEST-DESIGNER to build without design ambiguity?

This is a hard gate -- FAIL with specific, itemized gaps (per HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md's validator-fail worked example) if any check above doesn't pass; do not rubber-stamp.
acceptance_criteria: Verdict states explicitly, per ISS-0451 AC, whether AC1/AC2/AC3 are each covered by the design
Verdict states the validator's own independently re-derived arithmetic check result, not a repetition of CODE-DESIGNER's numbers
Verdict states explicitly whether any implementation code was found in the design doc
Verdict states explicitly whether REQ-219 AC2/AC4 preservation reasoning is checked and correct
A FAIL verdict lists every gap by section/line with what must change; a PASS verdict states what was independently re-derived and how
task.regate_note:
RE-GATE (iteration 3, SCOPED). This is not a full re-audit of the whole design -- the design itself (lib/letflow/design/iss0451-poller-crash-budget-isolation.md's mechanism, arithmetic, and production-code spec) already passed your gate clean at iteration 2 (gate_history[2]) and is not in question. What changed since then is narrower: ELIXIR-DEV's Step 3 implementation (handoffs/WF03-ISS0451-20260904/step-03-elixir-dev.json) surfaced a race in the design's OLD section 5 guidance for adapting the existing pollers_test.exs AC4 test -- full detail in that handoff's result.issues[0]. CODE-DESIGNER's iteration-3 revision (handoffs/WF03-ISS0451-20260904/step-02-code-designer.json, this run's own most recent result) rewrote section 5 to resolve it: the AC4 test no longer issues its own competing start_child/2 call at all -- it triggers with terminate_child/2 alone and polls PollersBreaker.breaker_state()/Process.whereis/1 until a new Pollers pid appears while breaker_state() == :closed, asserting the breaker never tripped for a single-shot fault. CODE-DESIGNER states explicitly this requires NO changes to lib/letflow/supervisor/pollers_breaker.ex or lib/letflow/application.ex.

Check, scoped to this change: (1) does the revised section 5 procedure actually resolve the specific race ELIXIR-DEV found (re-read their result.issues[0] and confirm the new procedure has no remaining competing-restart-call site); (2) is the new procedure concrete and unambiguous enough for ELIXIR-DEV to apply to test/letflow/supervisor/pollers_test.exs without inventing anything (exact calls, exact polling/assertion shape); (3) does it still prove what the ORIGINAL AC4 test proved (single Pollers-budget-exhaustion event leaves Infrastructure/Http/Repo untouched) -- REQ-219 AC4's own bar, not a weaker one; (4) is CODE-DESIGNER's claim of 'no production-code changes needed' actually correct, or does the new procedure secretly depend on something pollers_breaker.ex doesn't yet expose (breaker_state/0 was already specified at iteration 1 -- confirm it's still there and sufficient); (5) confirm no implementation code was added. If it holds up, PASS. If not, this is iteration 3 of 3 (the final rework) -- a further FAIL here means escalation per ORCHESTRATOR.md section 5, so be precise about whether a real gap remains or whether this passes.

gate_history.summary: Design's §4 margin arithmetic ('5 - 2 = 3') assumed PollersBreaker's terminate_child call always beat the top-level Supervisor's own automatic restart-on-exit for the same child crash. Independently re-derived and found unproven: no OTP guarantee that the breaker's monitor-message-then-synchronous-call chain completes before the top-level Supervisor's direct in-process EXIT reaction.
issues: BLOCKER: unproven race in the breaker's termination-vs-automatic-restart ordering, undermining AC2's arithmetic (full text in this run's git history, commit 4e127a7d).
gate_history.next_action: Rework CODE-DESIGNER -- either restart: :temporary on Pollers' child spec (removes race structurally) or cite an actual OTP ordering guarantee and re-derive the margin.

gate_history.summary: Rework iteration 1's fix (restart: :temporary via a {Letflow.Supervisor.Pollers, restart: :temporary} children-list entry) correctly diagnoses that :temporary would remove the race by construction, and correctly describes :temporary's OTP semantics (independently confirmed against lib/elixir/lib/supervisor.ex and a live probe on this project's pinned Elixir 1.20.3). But the specific children-list syntax used does not actually apply the :temporary override -- a 2-tuple {module, arg} children-list entry threads `arg` into the child's start_link call, not into Supervisor.child_spec/2's override keys, so the resulting child spec still defaults to :permanent. The original race from iteration 0 is therefore still live under this design as written.
issues: BLOCKER: §3.4a's `{Letflow.Supervisor.Pollers, restart: :temporary}` children-list syntax does not set restart: :temporary -- verified live that this exact form yields a child spec with no :restart override (Supervisor.child_spec/2's overrides parameter is never invoked by this syntax); the corrected form is `Supervisor.child_spec(Letflow.Supervisor.Pollers, restart: :temporary)` used as the children-list entry, confirmed live to work correctly.
BLOCKER: §3.6/§4's arithmetic and 'exactly 0 top-level restarts, structurally' claim depend on the broken syntax and are unproven as a result -- must be re-derived against the corrected snippet.

BLOCKER: §5's claim that the existing pollers_test.exs AC4 test 'will fail as written' is false under the design's actual (broken) syntax -- that test would keep passing, since the top level still auto-restarts Pollers today; must be restated once §3.4a is fixed.
BLOCKER: §6.2 step 6's `Process.whereis(Letflow.Supervisor.Pollers) == nil` observable is not reliably true under the broken syntax for the same reason.
gate_history.next_action: Rework CODE-DESIGNER -- fix §3.4a's children-list syntax to Supervisor.child_spec(Letflow.Supervisor.Pollers, restart: :temporary) (or equivalent explicit map form), then re-derive §3.6/§3.7/§4's arithmetic and restate §5/§6.2 step 6 against the corrected mechanism. Rework iteration 2 of 3.

gate_history.summary: Iteration 2 corrects §3.4a's children-list syntax to Supervisor.child_spec(Letflow.Supervisor.Pollers, restart: :temporary) and fixes the newly-discovered restart_child/2-vs-start_child/2 defect across every restart call site (PollersBreaker's :closed-branch and :half_open_probe handlers, plus the EXISTING pollers_test.exs's restart_pollers!/0 helper). Independently re-derived with full rigor, not a lighter pass: re-ran the corrected Supervisor.child_spec/2 probe live and confirmed it genuinely applies :temporary (the broken 2-tuple form does not); built a live top-level supervisor (max_restarts: 1) with a :temporary child and confirmed restart_child/2 on an already-exited :temporary child returns {:error, :not_found}, start_child/2 with the full spec correctly restarts it, terminate_child/2 on a :temporary child also deletes its spec, and 10 kill/start_child cycles never touched the top level's max_restarts:1 budget. Verified the design's citations of pollers_test.exs's actual current content (lines 99, 116-119, 152-161, 217-221) against the file itself, not the design's paraphrase -- all accurate. Re-checked §4's arithmetic (0-consumption invariant holds given the live-confirmed :temporary behavior), REQ-219 AC2/AC4 preservation (AC2 unaffected since :restart never governs start order; AC4's observable preserved, mechanism-change consequences for the existing test correctly and completely identified), and §6's regression-test spec for internal consistency now that restart_pollers!/0 itself needs replacing. No implementation code found -- the sole function body present is inside a throwaway probe module demonstrating OTP's own child_spec/2 semantics, not part of the PollersBreaker design.
